title: Canon medicinae / Avicenna, trans. Gerard of Cremona (BPL 7)
shelf_note: A 13th-century two-column Latin textualis manuscript of a surgical section (skull fractures) that matches the Canon in Gerard's version. No tradition or collection is set, so there is nothing to contradict.
structure_note: There are 255 printed backsteps and 268 repeats among 673 pages with a 'printed number'. This manuscript has no printed pagination; this leaf shows only a red mark at the head of column b. So those numbers are almost certainly misread marks or folio guesses, not a real broken sequence. structure.pages_translated is 0 while the pages_translated field says 901, so the counts disagree (E2). 948 of 1018 pages have OCR. The scan photographs the open volume: the leaf plus a strip of the facing page at the right edge.

pages.printed_marker: none legible: a small red mark at the head of column b, which I cannot read at this resolution (perhaps a quire or chapter sign)
pages.layout: two columns of Gothic textualis; red-underlined marginal rubric notes in the outer (left) margin; a strip of the facing page with its own red marginal note at the right edge

ocr_errors.ocr: aut fimus menilz greci possibilis est
ocr_errors.image: the opening lines of column a read as separate lines (roughly '…cum signis… de fractura' / '…et si est possibile. Et'); the OCR fuses them into one line that does not construe
ocr_errors.problem: Most of both columns is misread into Latin that does not construe. Lines are fused or dropped, and a reader of the transcription cannot recover what the page says. This is pervasive, not a few slips.

ocr_errors.ocr: et est via q iam dea. Et melz z aure
ocr_errors.image: the line appears once in column a
ocr_errors.problem: The OCR writes this line twice (lines 9 and 11 of its column a). The duplicate is not on the leaf.

ocr_errors.ocr: in fustera aut puluis in fudo fy ulino
ocr_errors.image: the leaf has one 'puluis in fundo … ulnis' line here; the next line on the image is a different line
ocr_errors.problem: A repeated line ('…puluis in fudo fy ulino') stands where a different line of the leaf belongs. That line is lost.

ocr_errors.image: marginal rubric reading approximately '…ar nō epulare' (non epulare)
ocr_errors.problem: The marginal note seems to carry a negation that the OCR reads as 'vulnus'. Low confidence at this resolution.

ocr_errors.image: the line ends with a red rubric after 'cepid.'
ocr_errors.problem: The red rubric at the foot of column a is left out

tr_errors.problem: The margin is translated from the misread; the leaf's note is about 'experientia'. It is marked unclear, which limits the harm.
If the image's 'nō' is right, the margin says the wound is NOT to be closed over before the bone is separated. The English states the opposite as fact. Low confidence.

tr_errors.source: z in etate qui eo rimoz magnus
tr_errors.english: in the season when the swelling is great
tr_errors.problem: 'in estate quia in eo timor magnus' (in summer, because then the danger is great) becomes a vague 'season' tied to a swelling. 'estate' (summer) is also rendered 'the season' a second time ('in the season … days'), which loses the summer/winter contrast with 'in winter' below.

other.note: A raw <column-break/> tag stands in the English reading text between the two halves
Most of the English consists of '<unclear>…</unclear>' fragments. This is honest about the OCR's state (and the <warning> says so), but the page as served is hardly readable.

items.quote: original: "capitale," that is, medicines for the head
a gum used to close wounds

missing.why: A general reader may take it literally; it is a red plant resin used as a drug
The dura mater (the membrane over the brain) is not named. A reader cannot tell what membrane the fracture rules refer to, here or in 'whether the fracture reaches the membrane'

book_verdict: This is the right leaf of a genuine Latin Avicenna manuscript, but the OCR of this page is largely garbled, with duplicated and dropped lines. The translation is honest about this and mostly shows '<unclear>' fragments, with a few moderate slips in the margins and with 'estate'. The notes and glosses that are there are sound.
